current_evidence: The 'Apply for planning permission' page links this PDF as the 'Planning validation list - printable version'. Its cover reads 'LOCAL VALIDATION LIST NOVEMBER 2025', which follows the consultation that ran 21 July to 1 September 2025 (council news, 18 July 2025), and searching found no later version.

issues.detail: The List date 2025-09-01 comes from PDF CreationDate metadata, which happens to match the day the consultation closed. The adopted list's cover is dated November 2025, so it should read 2025-11.
issues.evidence: Cover: 'STOKE-ON-TRENT CITY COUNCIL LOCAL VALIDATION LIST NOVEMBER 2025'

issues.detail: Householder is '(none)', but Section 2.1 Householders lists five local requirements. They are 4.6 Ecological Impact Assessment (likely effect on designated sites, important habitats or protected/priority species), 4.10 Flood Risk Assessment (Flood Zones 2/3, Zone 1 sites over 1ha, surface-water flood areas, Critical Drainage Areas), 4.11 Heritage Statement (affects a designated or non-designated heritage asset or its setting), 4.23 Sustainable Drainage Strategy, and 4.28 Tree Survey and Method Statement (trees on or next to the site that could be affected). Advertisement consent is also '(none)', but Section 2.8 requires 4.11 Heritage Statement and 4.15 Lighting Assessment (illuminated or digital adverts in sensitive locations).

The Works to trees rows are wrong. 'Planning Obligations / S106 Heads of Terms', 'Viability Assessment' and 'Waste / Refuse and recycling storage' were picked up only because their text sits just before the '2.7 Work to Trees' heading in the PDF. Section 2.7 actually requires 4.6 Ecological Impact Assessment and 4.28 Tree Survey and Method Statement, the latter always for works to trees. Listed building consent has 'Advertisement drawings / illumination details' and 'Lighting Assessment' rows taken from text next to the '2.9 Listed Building Consent' heading. Section 2.9 actually lists 4.3 Archaeological Assessment, 4.6 Ecological Impact Assessment and 4.22 Structural Survey, none of which Grokbot captured for LBC.
issues.evidence: Section 2.7 Work to Trees: 4.6, 4.28; Section 2.9 Listed Building Consent: 4.3, 4.6, 4.22

issues.detail: All roughly 40 non-householder rows are flagged 'INFERRED ... placed under Full planning', so the list's size tiers are lost. The source has separate tables for residential under 10 units, residential 10+ units, non-residential under 1,000 sqm, non-residential 1,000 sqm+, and Change of Use, which needs all of 4.1-4.31. Examples: Crime Impact Statement, Energy Statement and Landscape Plans apply only to 10+ units or 1,000 sqm/1ha+ non-residential, while Air Quality, Archaeology, Coal Mining and EV charging also apply to small schemes. Outline and Reserved matters are '(none)', but the source's development tables are not limited to full applications.

Some local requirements are missing or exist only under a wrong label. 4.20 Playing Field Land Assessment (development causing loss of, or prejudice to, playing field land) is not captured. 4.31 Waste Management Scheme Details (development involving the processing, transfer or deposition of waste) appears only as a mis-filed Works to trees row; the Full planning 'Waste' row instead describes bin storage. 4.9 Flood Risk Sequential and Exception Test is represented by a row whose excerpt is actually the town-centre sequential test. 4.5 Crime Impact Statement (10+ residential units, or 1,000 sqm/1ha+ non-residential) is represented by a row whose excerpt is the BNG text.

Many trigger excerpts run on into the next numbered item or carry the wrong item's text. Air Quality runs into 4.3 Archaeology, Archaeology into 4.4 Coal, Heritage into 4.12 Contamination, Travel Plan into 4.28 Tree Survey, and Daylight into 4.14 Landscape Plans. 'Crime prevention / Secured by Design' and 'BNG' share the same excerpt (BNG national text). 'Sequential / Exception Test (flood)' uses the town-centre sequential test. 'Schedule of works (listed building)' carries the 4.29 Ventilation/Extraction trigger. Structural Survey is truncated to 'possibility of land instability' and omits demolition of heritage or locally listed buildings, significant structural works to listed buildings, and rural building conversions. Flood Risk Assessment gives only 'In flood zone 2 or 3' and omits Zone 1 over 1ha, surface-water areas and Critical Drainage Areas over 0.5ha. Land Contamination omits the 10+ units, 1,000 sqm+ and previously developed land triggers.
issues.evidence: Section 4 Part One trigger tables (e.g. 4.22 Structural Survey; 4.10 Flood Risk Assessment)

issues.detail: Several rows are national requirements, guidance or boilerplate rather than local requirements. Block plan, Floor plans/Elevations, Roof plan, Sections/levels, Street scene, Design and Access Statement, Fire Statement and BNG are all in the source's Section 3 'National Requirements'. 'Pre-application advice / engagement details' is advice text from the Air Quality section. 'Highways / access details' ('All plans submitted should include Swept Path Analysis') is content guidance. 'Ground investigation / Geotechnical' and 'Daylight / Sunlight' are not headings in Section 4. The 'Submission rules' tab item ('The LPA often receive planning applications submitted with insufficient and poor quality information...') is introductory boilerplate.
issues.evidence: Section 3 headings '3.4 Site Plan / Block Plan', '3.10 Fire Statement', '3.11 Design & Access Statement', '3.12 Biodiversity Net Gain'

issues.detail: The source is internally inconsistent on the Affordable Housing Statement. Part Two says 15 or more residential units, but the Part One tables include it for residential schemes of 10+ units. Grokbot recorded only the 15-unit figure and did not flag the conflict.
issues.evidence: 4.1 Affordable Housing Statement: 'All applications for development involving 15 or more residential units' vs Table for residential 10+ units including 4.1

summary: Grokbot links the current November 2025 Stoke list but dated it from metadata (Sept 2025). It ignored the list's explicit per-application-type tables: Householder and Advertisement are marked '(none)' despite listed requirements, and the Works to trees and LBC rows are filled with neighbouring text. Many triggers run into the next item or belong to a different requirement.
